# Template — Buyer-Led Production Programme MOU (framework)

> ⚠️ **Template only.** This is a starting point for discussions, not legal advice.
> Both parties should have the final agreement reviewed by a lawyer or the relevant
> cooperative/association adviser before signing. Fill every `[bracket]`.

**Programme name:** `[e.g. 2027 white maize demand — Mahalapye cluster]`
**MOU date:** `[date]`

## Parties
1. **Buyer / programme sponsor:** `[organisation, registration no., physical & postal address, contact person, phone/email]`
2. **Producer(s):** `[farmer name / group name, address, contact]` (add schedule for multiple producers)
3. **Facilitator:** AgriSphere (via the programme board at `/programs.html`) — facilitator provides the platform, playbook and documentation layer only, and is **not a party to the sale contract**.

## 1. Product & volume
- Product: `[e.g. white maize, grade A]`
- Volume: `[e.g. 40 tonnes ± 10%]` season `[e.g. 2026/27]`
- Quality specs: `[attach or summarise: moisture %, purity, weevil freedom, size/weight, defect tolerance]`
- Delivery window & points: `[e.g. Feb–Mar 2027; BAMB depot X / buyer warehouse Y]`

## 2. Price formula (transparent & written)
- Formula: `[e.g. BAMB depot price in delivery week, plus P150/t quality bonus; floor of P3,000/t]`
- Weight/grading basis: `[e.g. official weighbridge / calibrated scale; joint grading with samples retained]`
- Adjustments: `[only those written here; no other deductions allowed]`

## 3. Advance & inputs
- Advance: `[e.g. 30% of estimated contract value within 14 days of signed contract]`
- Input credit (if any): `[e.g. certified seed supplied, deducted from final payment at documented cost]`
- Repayment of advance if crop fails: `[fair trigger agreed here, e.g. partial waiver where failure is weather-related and documented]`

## 4. Producer commitments
- Follow the stage-gated playbook and keep batch records (planting, treatments, harvest, storage) per AgriSphere traceability guidance.
- Meet quality specs and delivery schedule; notify buyer immediately of any risk to volume/quality.
- Sell contracted volume only to the buyer unless otherwise agreed in writing.

## 5. Buyer commitments (fair-terms checklist)
- Written contract to each producer, in language understood by the producer.
- Transparent price formula (above); no unfair deductions or hidden penalties.
- Advance/input terms honoured on schedule.
- Payment within `[e.g. 14]` days of accepted delivery; interest on late payment `[optional: state]`.
- Designated contact & dispute channel.

## 6. Delivery, acceptance & rejection
- Rejection only for documented failure of written specs, with samples retained by both parties.
- Disputed loads: independent grading by `[e.g. BAMB / agreed third party]`, cost shared.
- Documentation: delivery note, batch record, grading sheet per load.

## 7. Disputes
- Step 1: joint meeting within 7 days. Step 2: mediation via `[cooperative office / extension office / kgotla / agreed mediator]`. Step 3: lawful courts/arbitration of the producers' jurisdiction. Farmers' organisations may assist free of charge at any step.

## 8. Ethics & integrity
- Both parties commit to honest grading, truthful records, no bribery, no child labour, and fair treatment. Suspected fraud voids the affected portion and is reportable through AgriSphere's reporting channel.

## 9. Term & exit
- Programme runs `[start]` to `[end]`; either party may exit for material breach with 14 days' written notice and settlement of delivered volumes.
